summary: Judged the dead attempt-1 tree (its reshape/arange constexpr-shape fold in lower_tir.py, the multi-axis program_id decomposition, the fp16/bf16 math class, const-i1, the masked scalar load/store and the block bool load/store were sound and are kept; verified by probes before building on them) and completed the remaining small construct classes. All owned classes are at ZERO in the definitive filtered compile sweep over the 46 census operators carrying them (162 identities: 110 artifacts + 49 located refusals of OTHER constructs + 3 over-budget + 0 crash; docs/compiler-agent/COMPILE_CENSUS.t031-owned-classes.json): tl.reshape (runtime-shape forms fold -- block extents are compile-time in the pinned language; genuinely runtime bounds keep the located tl.arange.end/tl.reshape refusal, kept as a negative test), tl.arange.end, store/load i1 pointee, scalar bool loads/stores, const-i1, tl.softmax/erf/sqrt/rsqrt/floor/log, tl.program_id axis, masked scalar store, convert (int64->f32, fp64 internal routes). Repairs behind the zeros: (1) the bool backing-store lane -- scalar_store writes the scalar-bool GPR's low 0/1 byte (the dead attempt's convert_width crashed reading .width off a MaskType and refused 64->8), a rank-0 bool result of convert binds the scalar-bool i64 0/1 GPR convention instead of a mask, block vcmp unifies integer operands that agree in TIR but ride different lane widths (the 0/1 class at the data SEW vs the broadcast splat), and a 0/1 reduction class narrower than its merge accumulator widens to it (the e8 bool-storage pass feeding an i32 sum; also removes the e8 overflow risk); (2) per-chunk-partial wrong answers exposed by first execution -- a rank-0 top-level reduce consumed only inside the region now escapes through the region's own statements AND through runtime regions' carried values/joins (median_bool_dim_finish, std_dim_kernel_inner), the pass splits at the first consumer, the per-pass liveout tables no longer clobber the merged binding, and an in-pass region join consumed by a later pass now STAGES its lanes to the private workspace (the andor form went from a latent wrong answer to correct); (3) 16-bit float SCALAR binops/compares ride the fp32-lane policy (bf16 bits at the e16 lanes are fp16 on this target; blocked_jacobi/cyclic_jacobi bf16 now match the reference exactly: alpha*beta 103.0 vs the pre-fix 20224.0); (4) compile cost -- _value_by_vid is an indexed map and the allocator's weight build indexes defining blocks (complex_svd's lowering went from >590s to 4.6s, allocate from >234s to 13s; the sweep's slowest cold compile dropped from 94.8s to 23.3s). Executed-and-compared evidence: test_t031_repairs (8 checks, 1 and 4 workers, independent numpy references) all PASS; the full a100c test suite (36 files) all PASS; end-to-end execution of the owned operators: 131 cases PASS (bool stores round-trip exactly; the bf16/fp16 jacobi, std_dim, any/median/unique bool families all PASS), 4 mismatches remain in local_ne tile_sum (a reproduced design conflict in the masked-load-without-other default, filed below), 2 SIGILL launch failures and 3 k_new mismatches are first-execution exposures of the tl.dot lane (other constructs), 3 complex_svd stage timeouts (compile still ~216s vs the 120s budget after the cost fixes; pre-existing quadratic passes/verify cost). No construct moved to declared-unsupported: every owned class is inside the pinned Triton 3.8 subset (the reference audit passes all 2734 cases; my reference probes confirmed tl.softmax fp16/bf16 and the shape-derived arange/reshape forms are supported, and tl.sqrt/erf/floor/log/rsqrt on 16-bit operands only occur promoted to fp32 in the corpus), so FRONTEND_COVERAGE.json keeps all 107 rows implemented.

design_issue.observed_failure: local_ne_consecutive_kernel and local_ne_flat_impl ([17] and [97] int32, 4 cases) produce wrong tile_sum values (exact comparison fails): the kernels load with a mask but no `other` and then CONSUME the disabled lanes (tl.where(i0 > 0, a != b, 0) keeps the disabled lanes' loaded garbage; tl.sum adds them). These cases are validated on the pinned reference (the reference audit passes all 2734 cases), so the corpus's effective contract requires the disabled lanes to read as neutral.
design_issue.evidence: Reference probes (a100_support/run-reference.sh, pinned triton 3.8.0 CPU): a masked load without `other` feeding a sum yields the VALID-PREFIX value deterministically (16 == the 17-valid-lane prefix count; a plain sum yields 136 == the valid values' sum) -- the pinned reference zero-fills (or otherwise neutralizes) the undef lanes. My compiler's masked load declares default=undef and leaves the disabled lanes as the register's prior content, so the sum adds garbage. Reproduction: python3 tools/run_scan.py run --operator suite/dev/local_ne_flat_impl.py -> tile_sum_ptr exact comparison failed at both shapes.
design_issue.root_cause: A declared-design vs input-contract conflict: COMPILER_ARCHITECTURE.md section 2.2 declares 'masked load without other is undefined at disabled positions -- never zero-filled' (the MIR records MaskedDefault.UNDEF), while the corpus's validated cases depend on the pinned reference's deterministic zero at disabled lanes. The reviewed ARCHITECTURE_CONSTRAINTS.json only requires no-out-of-range-access at disabled positions (preserved either way); the conflict is with the architecture narrative's undef sentence and with any consumer that reads undef lanes.
design_issue.proposed_change: Materialize the UNDEF default as 0 at disabled lanes in the vector load lowering (a vsel with zero after the undef vunit_load/vloadix, exactly like the declared VALUE-0 default) -- matching the pinned reference's observable behavior; the TIR/MIR still RECORD the UNDEF distinction, and the no-access invariant is unchanged. Update the COMPILER_ARCHITECTURE.md 2.2 sentence accordingly (undef loads deterministically read 0 on this target, matching the pinned reference) and add an executed regression test (the local_ne form).
